title: Avoiding secrets in browser bundles
learningObjectives: Explain avoiding secrets in browser bundles and apply secure, accessible, maintainable browser practices.

understand.concept: All JavaScript, HTML, source maps, and network traffic delivered to a browser can be inspected. Private keys, service-account credentials, signing secrets, and privileged tokens must stay on trusted servers. Public provider keys require restrictions and monitoring where applicable.
understand.whyItMatters: Minification and obfuscation do not protect secrets. A leaked credential can be copied and abused; use server-side secret storage, least privilege, rotation, and monitoring.
understand.analogy: Anything shipped to the browser is effectively public, even if its name looks obscure.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser security, accessibility, and performance rules depend on platform behaviour and server configuration.

explain.narrative: The example contains ordinary public configuration. Privileged credentials must be used only in a trusted backend.

examples.code: const publicSettings={apiBase:'/api',theme:'light'};console.log(publicSettings.apiBase);// Never include private service credentials in this bundle.
examples.explanation: The example contains ordinary public configuration. Privileged credentials must be used only in a trusted backend.
examples.expectedOutput: Browser console or UI output demonstrates the security or reliability principle.

practise.guidedTask: Review a sample frontend config and classify each value as public configuration or a secret. Move secrets behind a server API.
practise.independentTask: Review a small browser feature for security, accessibility, performance, and lifecycle risks. Add a fallback and document the server-side controls required.
hints: Treat all browser and network input as untrusted.
Use exact origin checks and least privilege.
Measure performance and clean up resources.

questions.answer: No, browser-delivered code can be inspected

Assume all browser features are always available
questions.answer: Defence in depth, least privilege, and usable fallbacks
questions.explanation: Secure and reliable interfaces combine trusted server enforcement with careful client behaviour.
